checkpoints: An edit causes no store write before its document’s 120 ms quiet interval expires.
Multiple edits to one document within the quiet interval produce exactly one write containing the latest text.
After one burst saves, a later burst for the same document schedules and completes another save.
Pending edits for different document IDs use independent trailing tasks.
Navigate or close before expiry: the pending document save still completes, while its retired badge subscription receives no status update.
If a synchronous store listener navigates during a delayed save, that navigation remains current after the save callback returns.
The search preview retains its independent 40 ms trailing behavior and hide cancellation.
Public JavaScript source remains syntactically valid after any Action.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue writing to the store on every keystroke.
Do not publish intermediate text from within one editing burst.
Do not share one trailing timer/value across different document IDs.
Do not cancel a document’s pending save merely because its view badge is replaced, closed, or disposed.
Do not let a delayed save restore or mutate a stale view after a synchronous listener navigates.
Do not change search-preview timing, publication, or hide behavior.
Do not change public method names, arguments, event names, source IDs/text, or store status payload semantics.
lifecycle_identity: A document trailing task is owned by BufferBank and identified by document ID within one coordinator instance.
Repeated visits to the same document ID reuse that document’s trailing task, allowing later bursts to save.
Different document IDs have distinct trailing-task state and quiet intervals.
The current view badge owns only its live store subscription; it does not own the document buffer or pending save.
The search preview owns a separate trailing task with its existing 40 ms interval.

obligations.text: When edit(text) is invoked with an active view, submit text to that view document’s existing trailing task instead of writing immediately to the store.
For edits to the same document within a burst, restart the 120 ms quiet interval and retain only the latest text.
When the quiet interval completes, write exactly the retained document ID and latest text to the store.
After a burst flushes, clear its pending state so later edits can schedule and save subsequent bursts.
Keep document-buffer lifetime independent of current-view badge retirement, including navigation, close, and dispose.
Preserve current-view subscription behavior: only the live subscribed view receives matching store status events.
Preserve synchronous navigation performed by store listeners during a delayed save; the save completion must not overwrite the resulting view state.
Preserve createWorkspace open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(), its scoped event interfaces, and createSearchPreview query(text), hide().
Leave the adjacent search preview unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Each active-view edit must reach the document trailing task before any save for that edit can occur.
For a document burst, every edit before expiry cancels/replaces the prior scheduled ticket; only 120 ms of quiet permits the retained value to flush.
The trailing task retires its ticket/value before invoking the store-writing consumer, permitting synchronous reentry and future scheduling.
View retirement removes the old live subscription before later pending document saves can publish status.
A synchronous navigation initiated by store notification takes precedence over any stale outer operation; no continuation may restore the prior view.
preservation: Inactive-view edit remains a no-op.
Opening still retires the prior view, installs a matching-ID status subscription, updates the view badge, and renders the document using the store’s current value.
Closing and disposing still retire the current view; workspace disposal still removes scoped handlers and view data.
Store read/write/subscribe remains synchronous, including its original event payload and revision semantics.
Document buffers continue to be owned separately from live Badge subscriptions.
Search preview remains transient, uses its different 40 ms quiet interval, and hide cancels its pending task.
All original source identities, text values, and status payloads retain their semantics.

No tests, configuration, dependencies, scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests are in scope.

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled.

Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

class BufferBank {constructor(){this.entries=new Map();}get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}}
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));

return{open:id=>node.triggerHandler('draft:open.scope',[id]),edit:t=>node.triggerHandler('draft:edit.scope',[t]),close:()=>node.triggerHandler('draft:close.scope'),dispose(){api.dispose();node.off('.scope');node.removeData('view');}};
